Chambers is one of those rare places that gets everything right — every single time.

The space is just incredibly pleasant: great energy, perfect music level, beautifully lit without being too dark or too bright. It’s the kind of place where you immediately feel good.

The wine list alone is worth the visit — incredibly sharp, deep, and very well priced. And the team really knows what they’re doing. Pascaline is outstanding, and even when she’s not there, the sommeliers are consistently excellent. Jared and the team run this place flawlessly.

The food is just as impressive. The menu is short but extremely well thought out, with great products and a real sense of creativity. There are a few staples you can always rely on (the chicken, the cavatelli, the mascarpone millefeuille), but I usually try something new every time — and it’s always a win.

Honestly, there’s nothing to criticize. Food, wine, atmosphere, service — it’s just a perfect restaurant. Highly recommend.

Solo dinner at the bar, and honestly one of the easiest recommendations I've made in a while — you step off the Chambers St station and you're basically there. Chambers is unapologetically wine-forward: a thick binder of special pours, low lighting, marble bar, and bartenders who actually want to talk about what's in your glass. For my DC people, picture Reveler's Hour's wine program merged with Rye Bunny's kitchen and you're close. It's the kind of room where dining alone at the bar feels like the correct way to do it, not the consolation prize.

The food holds its own against the wine list. Veal sweetbreads with Tokyo turnips and garlic chives were the standout — that soft, bouncy sweetbread texture against the crisp snap of turnip, with freshly ground black pepper doing quiet work against the gaminess. I asked for a pairing and got a Central California chardonnay blend with chenin in it, a smart, slightly nerdy pour. The Berkshire pork loin with kohlrabi, fennel, and mustard came next, matched with an Alsatian blend from Binner whose high acidity cut straight through the fattiness of the pork. These are pairings that feel thought through, not recited.

Ended on a pavlova with apricots — light, tangy, very summery — and treated myself to a glass of 2016 Dolcetto d'Alba from Rivella Serafino, a tiny Barbaresco grower whose serious, small-production nebbiolo has a cult following; getting their Dolcetto by the glass tells you everything about how this list is built. Chambers is what a neighborhood wine restaurant should be: real cooking, a deep and personal wine program, and a bar seat that treats solo diners like regulars. I'll be back next time I'm in Tribeca.

The menu is nothing short of masterful. Every dish tastes like it was crafted by someone who truly knows and loves Italian food from rich, velvety pastas to tender, perfectly seasoned entrées. The Ravioli Zucca practically melts on your tongue, and the Brasato di Costolette di Manzo (braised short ribs) is pure comfort elevated to art.

But what really sets Gabriels apart isn’t just the food its the experience. The ambiance strikes a beautiful balance between cozy and elegant, ideal for a romantic dinner, a pre-theater meal before Lincoln Center, or a weekend brunch with friends.   The staff are consummate professionals warm, attentive, and genuinely invested in making your meal memorable. I’ve never felt rushed or overlooked; instead, every detail feels thoughtfully executed.

Do yourself a favor and dine here, it is SO good. I already can't wait to go back.

Indian Accent

I walked into the restaurant expecting a typical messy Indian buffet. That’s not what I got.
It is a hot day and I’m wearing shorts and a t shirt and I am woefully underdressed. The crowd is dressed nicely, and looks like they must work in the area. The decor is sophisticated, with gold and beige walls and a high ceiling. Jazz on the playlist.

The amuse bouche was a delicious soup accompanied by some strange dumplings filled with some kind of cheese. The first ordered dish was a white sweet potato with star fruit. The second was a paneer, but prepared in an unusual way. The dessert was a black rice pudding and cake with almonds and rose petals.

I’ve been eating Indian food for about 50 years and I have never seen these dishes. Innovative and tasty with impeccable service.
A great restaurant.

The food at Indian Accent was undoubtedly well prepared, beautifully presented, and full of interesting flavors. The service was also professional and attentive throughout the meal.

That said, I left feeling somewhat disappointed by the overall dining format. Couple of dishes were absolutely avoidable and tasted as if made at home. For a restaurant positioned as a premium tasting experience, the portions are extremely small, which makes the meal feel less satisfying than expected.

My biggest criticism is the menu structure itself. Having to choose just one dish from each course category feels limiting, especially when there are so many interesting options on offer. Part of the appeal of a restaurant like this is exploring a range of flavors and signature creations, but the format prevents guests from getting a truly well-rounded experience unless they return multiple times. Given the portion sizes, it can feel like you're paying for the opportunity to choose rather than actually experience the breadth of the menu.

It's a good restaurant with talented chefs, but the combination of very small portions and a restrictive tasting format took away from what could have been a much more memorable dining experience.

Quality Bistro continues to be one of our absolute favorite restaurants in the city. We’ve dined here many times over the years, and there’s a reason we keep coming back—the service is consistently impeccable, the food is fresh and beautifully executed, and the romantic atmosphere has a certain NYC magic that’s hard to replicate.

This time we started with several crudos, and the Yellowtail with hibiscus and raspberry and Montauk Fluke with grapefruit and elderflower were standouts—bright, delicate, and beautifully balanced. The Soft Shell Crab was fantastic, and the Steak Tartare Tartine is absolutely worth ordering.

For mains, the Seared Halibut with coconut nage was beautifully cooked, while the Pork Porterhouse with roasted pineapple was rich and memorable. Definitely add the Maitake Mushrooms, Macaroni & Cheese Gratin, and Spicy Carrots à l’Orange for the table.

We finished with the Espresso Crème Brûlée and Strawberries & Sweet Cream—the perfect ending to another wonderful dinner.

Quality Bistro remains one of those places we recommend without hesitation. Great food, beautiful atmosphere, and exceptional hospitality every time. Make your reservation in advance—it gets busy quickly, and for good reason

I went to a French restaurant to celebrate my birthday. When my boyfriend made the reservation, he mentioned it was my birthday, but the restaurant didn’t do anything special for it—which was a little disappointing.

That said, the food was really good. The flavors were just right, and the prices felt reasonable for the portion sizes. The only thing was that his steak came with a huge amount of fries—way more than the steak itself—while the salad was just a few leaves. It would’ve been nicer (and looked better too) with a bit more salad for balance.
The crème brûlée had subtle notes of rum and citrus (might be wrong) and wasn’t too sweet - it was probably my favorite crème brûlée.

It was a busy weekend night, so the place was pretty crowded. The restaurant is on the smaller side, and at our little two-person bistro table, we kept getting bumped by the chairs behind us, which made it a bit uncomfortable. It also would’ve been great if there were hooks at the table to hang bags.

Overall, we had a nice time, but a few small things could’ve made the experience even better.

We loved their 99$ menu option for 2 people.

Our fav dishes were:
- Baerng Golae (S): Coconut crisp, grilled shrimp, and famous curry paste from southern Thailand.
- Squid Ink Fried Rice: Fried rice, colossal crab meat, egg, and squid with the aromatic squid ink sauce, fried garlic, cucumber, and cilantro come with prik nam pla.

The crab curry was too hot (according the waitress it’s 7/10 spicy but it ended up feeling like way more for someone who never has hot food).

The veggies were very well cooked.

The Yum Som-O (Fresh Pomelo, fried cured branzino, chili, lemongrass shallot, mint, cilantro with nahm pla whan dressing) was fresh and sweet and we loved every bite! The only thing that surprised us is that the pieces of fish were way smaller than they appear in their website.

Finally, the atmosphere was great! It’s wasn’t too loud, too cold/hot, too dark. It was perfect.

The waitresses were fast and kind. We had booked a table for 2 and we had indicated that we didn’t want to sit right under the AC and when we arrived that’s the table we got. We asked them to change and they quickly adapted.

No complaints, we will come back!!

The sauce was slightly tangy and a perfect accompaniment to the Argentinian shrimp. We also had our reliable starter: the carciofi e calamari fritti (baby artichokes and calamari gently fried and served with a zesty dip).
For entrees, we had their housemade spinach ravioli (perfectly al dente, with butter & sage sauce) and a grilled swordfish special. I requested medium rare-medium and out came a delicious piece of fish served with asparagus & capers.
They have a nice selection of wines by the bottle and glass (I had a new Albarino white wine) and we love the classic & spicy margaritas.
We opted for cappucino instead of dessert this time around (we were stuffed!) and, as always, it was excellent.
Thank you, Henry & Ruri, for continuing the great Felice tradition of great food and inviting spaces.

We recently celebrated my older sister’s birthday at Hutong, and overall it was a very memorable experience. We reserved one of the private dining rooms for our family, and it made the celebration feel so much more intimate and special. The room was elegant, quiet, and beautifully designed, allowing us to enjoy quality time together without feeling rushed or surrounded by too much noise. The view was honestly one of the biggest highlights of the entire evening. Looking out at the city while celebrating such an important occasion created unforgettable memories, and the atmosphere alone made the night feel luxurious.

I also want to compliment the staff because the service was truly exceptional from beginning to end. Everyone was professional, friendly, attentive, and made sure we were well taken care of throughout the entire dinner. They frequently checked on our table, made sure our drinks were always refilled, answered every question we had about the menu, and helped everything run smoothly. They made my sister feel celebrated on her birthday, and our family really appreciated the extra care and attention they gave us.

As for the food, you can definitely tell the ingredients are high quality and beautifully presented. Every dish looked like a piece of art, and the presentation was outstanding. Some dishes were absolutely delicious, while others weren’t quite to our personal taste. Since Hutong specializes in Sichuan cuisine, many of the dishes had a strong spicy flavor. We had a fantastic dinner at Hutong and truly enjoyed the entire experience. The restaurant is tucked inside Beacon Courtyard, which gives it a stylish and elegant atmosphere away from the busy streets of Midtown. The dining room is beautiful and perfect for a date night, celebration, or dinner with friends.

The seared scallops were perfectly cooked—lightly caramelized on the outside while remaining soft and tender inside. They paired surprisingly well with the spicy soba noodles and sesame peppercorn sauce.

The Peking duck was definitely one of the highlights of the evening. The skin was crispy, the meat was juicy, and everything tasted delicious wrapped in the thin pancakes with the traditional accompaniments. The green peppercorn fish was delicate and tender, with a fragrant numbing flavor that was not overpowering.

We also loved the Ma La prawns and beef tenderloin. The prawns were plump and packed with Sichuan peppercorn, garlic, and ginger flavors. The beef tenderloin was incredibly tender and savory, with black beans, red peppercorns, chili, and Chinese celery. Both dishes went perfectly with the chef’s fried rice, which was flavorful without being greasy.

Dessert was another pleasant surprise. The Hong Kong milk tea tiramisu was creamy, fragrant, and not overly sweet, while the soy milk cheesecake had a smooth texture and a lovely nutty flavor.

Beautiful atmosphere, attentive service, creative cocktails, and consistently delicious food from beginning to end. We had a wonderful experience and will definitely return!

For appetizers, we shared the **Calamar et Courgette Frits** and the **Torchon de Foie Gras de Maison**. The calamari was perfectly crisp and light, while the foie gras torchon with tomato chutney and brioche was rich, decadent, and absolutely delicious.

Oh!! & let's not forget the espresso Martini we had after dessert. It was the perfect after dinner drink.

I can't wait to return ✨

Empellón was fantastic, and I would absolutely come back. We came in for an early dinner on a Friday and had a truly wonderful meal from start to finish.

We started with the guacamole with 7 salsas, which came highly recommended — and it absolutely lived up to the hype. This is a must-order. Best part? There’s plenty left over to use throughout the rest of the meal.

We then shared the fish tempura tacos and the rib steak fajita, and while the tacos were good, they were completely overshadowed by the fajitas. The fajita plate was outstanding — 20 ounces of perfectly tender steak, fresh warm corn tortillas, and a deeply flavorful bone marrow that tied everything together beautifully.

We finished with the very popular avocado dessert, which was the perfect way to end the meal. It wasn’t heavy or overly sweet and came with these wonderful petit fours filled with ice cream that tasted like a key lime crust — such a thoughtful, refreshing finale.

Shoutout to our waiter, who made the experience even better — fun, kind, attentive, and genuinely made us feel taken care of.

Overall, an excellent meal with bold flavors, thoughtful execution, and great service. I’d absolutely come back to explore more of their modern menu.

The standout was the XO scallop roll: easily the most interesting in terms of flavour and ingredients, and I’d come back just for that. The other rolls were good too, but I’d hoped the inventive flavours and ideas would carry through the whole menu, and that creativity sort of tapered off after the scallop roll.

That said, it felt fairly priced for the experience, so I walked away feeling like I got real value out of the meal.

This was my first time visiting Nami Nori, and it blew me away. I ordered the Signature Temaki Set and paired it with the Kato Sake, which was a flawless combination. Every single handroll was spectacular, but if I had to rank my favorites, the X.O. scallop took the top spot, followed closely by the tuna poke, salmon serrano, cucumber black sesame, and the coconut shrimp.
The XO Scallop features perfectly tender, sweet scallops enhanced by the deeply savory, complex heat of the house-made XO sauce. It provides an excellent umami depth without overpowering the delicate seafood.Equally impressive is the Tuna Poke, which offers a refreshing, clean flavor profile. The tuna is exceptionally fresh, dressed in a well-balanced marinade that highlights the quality of the fish.
What truly elevated the night was the service. When I told the server it was my first time, she went above and beyond. She patiently explained the menu, gave fantastic recommendations, and stayed incredibly attentive throughout the entire meal without ever being intrusive. I cannot wait to come back!

From start to finish, this restaurant delivered an unforgettable dining experience. The staff guided us expertly through the menu, making excellent recommendations that truly elevated our meal.

What made this visit truly unique was the innovative presentation of their temaki (hand rolls). They arrive warm and crispy in a beautiful wooden box, and you grab each one individually as you eat—it's a fun, interactive, and delicious way to enjoy sushi. The freshness and quality of every piece was outstanding, and the crispy nori shells were perfectly executed.

The combination of impeccable service, creative menu options, and this distinctive serving style made for a memorable night. The staff's knowledge and attention to detail really shines through in every aspect of the experience.

Highly recommend—a must-visit for anyone who loves fresh, expertly-prepared sushi!

text.text:
While visiting NY, our daughter wanted to have lunch with our niece at a Thai restaurant, I and my wife just followed. It's a very crowded place and people are waiting for a long time. We had to wait so I went to get some coffee. No drinks from outside, so when the time for us to sit, I had to stayed outside to finish my just bought coffee before coming in.
The restaurant is packed and the tables are small but very cozy IMHO.
Again, my daughter ordered everything. I was just there to eat.
The service is quite fast and attentive because people are waiting outside, although they don't rush us to finish our lunch.
All the dishes are very tasty and excellent, the portions are not bad.
The lobster fettuccine is excellent, very flavorful.
The coconut chicken is different  and good too.
The Green curry fried rice is very delicious.
All the dishes in this restaurant are very tasty and the prices are reasonable, no wonder the restaurant is so crowded. I'm not crazy about Thai cuisine, but this one is not really traditional Thai to me, so I really liked it. We will come back here next time we visit our daughter.

We came here for lunch and two of us got the lobster noodles, french toast, chicken liver, and morning glory. The morning glory was super flavorful, and the chicken liver was really good with the peanuts and savory seasoning.

My favorite was definitely the French toast. I thought the dark filling inside was chocolate at first, but it turned out to be condensed brown sugar. It was sooo good! The toast had a great texture, and the Thai butter on the side made it even better. The lobster noodles was not that good tho. They weren’t bad but they were probably our least favorite dish and nothing really stood out about them. And the staff was super friendly and so welcoming!

text.text:
If you ever loved Uncle Boons, Thai Diner will definitely feel familiar—but it doesn’t quite hit the same highs. Service was fast and attentive, which set a great tone, but the food ended up being pretty hit or miss. The som tum salad was a standout and easily one of the best things on the menu—bright, balanced, and genuinely exciting. The crab fried rice had excellent texture and plenty of fresh crab, but the flavor just didn’t have that same depth Boons used to deliver.

The mussels and fries were a mixed bag: fries were perfectly seasoned and crisp, and the mussels were clean, but the sauce felt one-note and the sweet pickled onions threw the whole dish off. The fried snapper was cooked well but leaned overly sweet—I’d definitely order the sauce on the side next time so it doesn’t overpower everything. The accompanying rice was a miss: under-seasoned, mushy, and mixed with large pieces of herbs and cucumbers that didn’t quite work due to the texture of the rice. The spicy tamarind margarita also skewed too sweet.

That said, the coconut sundae was incredible and honestly worth coming back for on its own. Overall, I’d come back for the nostalgia (and dessert).

I ended up at Thai Diner after wandering around Nolita for a while and looking for somewhere that felt casual but memorable. The place was busy without feeling chaotic, and once the food started arriving I understood why people keep coming back. I started with the khao soi, which came out steaming hot with a rich curry broth and noodles that somehow stayed perfectly textured all the way through the meal. It was comforting without feeling heavy.

I also ordered the Thai disco fries because they sounded too interesting to pass up. They were crispy underneath and covered with a flavorful curry sauce that made them disappear much faster than expected. The chicken satay had a nice char from the grill and paired well with the peanut sauce, while the roti was soft and perfect for scooping up every bit of curry left on the plate.

What I liked most was that nothing felt overly complicated. The flavors were bold but approachable, and every dish felt like something you would happily order again. By the end of the meal I was already looking around at other tables wondering what I should try next time.
